title: The Illusion of Being Too Busy
script: Narrator: [wry] For years I wore busyness like a badge, as though a packed schedule were proof that my life mattered somehow.
Narrator: [reflective] Every conversation seemed to circle back to how little time I had, which, looking back, was a peculiar thing to boast about.
Narrator: [honest] What unsettled me was a weekend I spent entirely alone, with no obligations, and I genuinely didn't know what to do with myself.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I'd filled every hour for so long that unstructured time felt less like rest and more like an ambush.
Narrator: [analytical] So I started tracking my actual hours, rather than my perceived ones, and the results were quietly humbling.
Narrator: [wry] A great deal of what I'd labelled essential turned out to be scrolling disguised as research, or errands that could easily have waited.
Narrator: [honest] I wasn't as overwhelmed as I'd assumed; I was simply avoiding stillness, because stillness left room for questions I hadn't wanted to answer.
Narrator: [reflective] Once I admitted that, the busyness lost its usual disguise, and I could finally see it for what it was: a distraction dressed up as productivity.
Narrator: [determined] I began blocking out two unscheduled hours each week, which sounds trivial, yet initially felt almost transgressive to protect.
Narrator: [honest] The first few attempts were uncomfortable. I'd hover near my phone, itching for something, anything, to fill the silence.
Narrator: [warmly] Gradually, though, that discomfort softened into something closer to relief, as if I'd finally been given permission to simply exist.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I've since noticed how many people around me perform busyness the same way I used to, wearing exhaustion as a kind of credential.
Narrator: [gentle] I no longer envy that version of myself, constantly in motion yet strangely unable to say what any of it was actually for.
Narrator: [encouraging] If your calendar is full but your reasons for filling it are vague, it might be worth asking what you're actually avoiding.

quiz.question: How did the narrator use to treat busyness?
options: As a badge, proof that her life mattered
As something to hide from others
quiz.explanation: She says she wore busyness like a badge, as proof that her life mattered.

quiz.question: What experience first unsettled her?
options: A weekend entirely alone with no obligations, not knowing what to do
quiz.explanation: A weekend spent alone with no obligations left her not knowing what to do with herself.

quiz.question: What did she discover when she tracked her actual hours?
options: She had no free time at all
Much of what she called essential was scrolling or errands that could have waited
quiz.explanation: She found that much of her supposedly essential time was scrolling disguised as research or unnecessary errands.

quiz.question: What does the narrator conclude she was actually avoiding through busyness?
options: Stillness, because it left room for questions she hadn't wanted to answer
quiz.explanation: She realizes she was avoiding stillness because it left room for uncomfortable questions.

quiz.question: What change did she eventually make?
options: She began blocking out two unscheduled hours each week
She deleted all her apps permanently
She moved to a new city
quiz.explanation: She started deliberately protecting two unscheduled hours each week.
